clue.text: Delicate tennis shot to end barrage

parts.note: to end something is to stop it
a barrage of shots or questions is a volley

explanation.surface: A player calls for a soft drop at the net to halt a fierce rally of hard hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a gentle volley that drops just over the net with little bounce is known by this name.

clue.text: Band, southern, has reformed

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of has are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A musical group from the south has got back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a pop group re-forming, but it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Just left out by variety of agate

indicators.note: out says the left abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: just means only, as in just one
by is the multiplication sign, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A particular agate gem has simply been omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded form of chalcedony, classed as a variety of agate.

clue.text: Australian state having choice fruit

parts.note: Victoria is a state in south-east Australia
plum means choice or highly desirable, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: An Australian state boasting excellent produce.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a popular English variety of plum, oval and red-yellow, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Gain knowledge of Shakespearean king and knight

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of a Shakespeare tragedy
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Studying a Shakespeare play about a monarch and a chivalrous knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain knowledge of a subject is to study it and come to know it.

clue.text: Watch programme that includes commercial for a cosmetic

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it

indicators.note: that includes means the programme word holds the commercial inside it

parts.note: a TV programme is a show
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Viewers watch a show whose ad break promotes a beauty product.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coloured make-up applied to the eyelids, so a cosmetic.

clue.text: Sign of injury may cause a good deal of alarm

indicators.note: a good deal of a word is most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to alarm someone is to scare them

explanation.surface: A visible wound might well frighten onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on the skin after a wound heals is the lasting sign that an injury happened.

clue.text: Jazz musician, number one in foundation

parts.note: a count is a number or total

indicators.note: in places the one inside the foundation word

parts.note: a base is a foundation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A top jazz player is the cornerstone of the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie was an American jazz pianist and big-band leader.

clue.text: Practice gallop finished

parts.note: a gallop is a fast run
through means finished, as in we are through

explanation.surface: A horse's training canter is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial performance of something from start to end is practice.

clue.text: Tight spot right beside broadcaster's building

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster; the 's is read as 'is'
a scrape is an awkward or tight situation

explanation.surface: A TV company finds itself in difficulty next to its own tall headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall multi-storey tower is a kind of building.

clue.text: Spell "vase" after bit of tuition

indicators.note: after places the vase word behind the bit of tuition
a bit of the word tuition is taken to mean its first letter

parts.note: an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: A pupil is taught to write the word vase in a short lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like a request to spell out a word, but it means a stint or go.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell or a go at something is a stint taken in rotation with others.

clue.text: Solicitors' mail?

parts.note: solicitors here are not lawyers but things that solicit: letters sent on that each beg the recipient to copy and send more

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitors' suggests lawyers (British solicitors are a kind of lawyer), but here it means things that solicit, letters that demand to be passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Such letters are posted in a growing sequence, each pleading with recipients to send copies on.

clue.text: Cheers below deck?

definitions.meaning: a drinking toast said before downing a glass
on a ship, going through the hatch takes you down to the lower decks

explanation.surface: A sailor raises a glass while going down below on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a jokey toast urging a drink be swallowed, and literally describes passing through a ship's hatchway downward.

clue.text: Daily row about golf figure who's less powerful than he looks?

definitions.text: figure who's less powerful than he looks?

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper, a paper

indicators.note: about means the row word goes round the golf letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newspaper's quarrel with a golfing personality who is weaker than he seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface primes Tiger Woods as the golf figure, but the definition is the idiom for an empty threat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone or something that appears threatening but is actually ineffectual.

clue.text: Massive memorial by a lake

parts.note: a monument is a memorial
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A huge commemorative structure standing beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something massive is enormous in scale, like a great memorial building.

clue.text: A nasty boil removed, got rid of

indicators.note: nasty suggests the boil has been messed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to shed something is to remove or cast it off

explanation.surface: An unpleasant boil has been taken off and is now gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something entirely, the same as getting rid of it.

clue.text: Tall story swallowed by others abroad who offer accommodation?

indicators.note: swallowed by means the tall story sits inside the scrambled letters
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of others are rearranged

parts.note: a tall story is a lie

explanation.surface: Fibbing travellers overseas tell a whopper.
explanation.definitionFit: People who run hotels provide lodging for paying guests, hence accommodation.

clue.text: State papers seen by a hospital close to Chicago

parts.note: identity papers are ID
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: the close of Chicago is its final letter

explanation.surface: Documents from a medical centre near Chicago are examined.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Stock English remark that's funny

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A typical British comment that happens to be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' reads as an adjective (a stock remark) but is the verb meaning to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a place with what it needs is to supply or furnish it with gear.

clue.text: Terry, thoroughly at home wearing short Roman garment

indicators.note: wearing means the shortened garment is wrapped around the other pieces
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the toga was the robe of a Roman citizen
well means thoroughly, as in well cooked
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man named Terry relaxes at home dressed in a skimpy toga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terry' looks like a man's name, but terry is a looped cotton fabric used for towels.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry cloth is the absorbent looped cotton fabric that bath towels are made from.

clue.text: Everything you'd expect in article by complete Scottish golfer?

parts.note: the is the definite article
full means complete
Colin Montgomerie, the Scottish golfer, is nicknamed Monty

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece offering the complete story of a Scottish golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the whole lot, every expected element included, with nothing held back.

clue.text: Nothing charged for fruit

parts.note: O resembles zero, nothing
a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: Free of charge for a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a price, but means electrically live.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Fabric: expert after lengths

indicators.note: after puts the expert word behind the length letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for length
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A cloth specialist is called in once the measurements are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork fabric made of thread in patterns.

clue.text: Wager about singular former football star

indicators.note: about means the wager word wraps round the singular letter

parts.note: a wager is a bet
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A punter bets on one ex-footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was a celebrated Northern Irish footballer of Manchester United in the 1960s.

clue.text: Barrier in the Tagus knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something blocking the river Tagus has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is what signals that the letters are concealed within 'the Tagus', so it is the hiding indicator here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged barrier that closes an opening in a fence or wall is a gate.

clue.text: Consider intentional

definitions.meaning: a verb: to think something over carefully

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to weigh things up; as an adjective it means done on purpose.

clue.text: Function of list, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than seen, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Someone asks what purpose a register of names is said to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A function someone performs in an organisation is their part or job there.

clue.text: Evaluation fools blokes in street

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: in places the blokes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: A judgement on a group of idiotic men out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation is a formal judgement of worth or quality, such as an exam or appraisal.
